items.title: Chrona 03: configurable data location and Chrona-owned namespace with organization manifests (CHX-DATALOC-001, CHX-024..027)
items.description: Depends on arca slice 2 (data location, ARCA-LOC) and arca slice 3 (record format, ARCA-REC) (data location and record format). New requirement CHX-DATALOC-001 (docs/requirements/CHRONA-DATA-LOCATION.md, user decision 2026-10-08): the data repository is configured per deployment and never hard-coded; Chrona creates and owns its namespace and never assumes it is the only application in the repository; Chrona's data must be separable under different permissions from other applications (for example Summa), which means deploying against its own repository, because GitHub permissions are per repository; no at-rest encryption for now. Also: organization folders with immutable OrganizationIds, the organization manifest (CHX-026), and public-repository refusal for production (CHX-027).

items.title: Chrona 04: GitHub sign-in through Fides and token safety (CHX-022, CHX-023)
items.description: Depends on fides slice 7 (WASM client and Arca token provider, FID-CLI) (WASM client and Arca token provider) and arca slice 5 (token-provider port, ARCA-AUTH) (token-provider port). Sign in through Fides (GitHub only for now). Resolve the identity from GitHub, never a typed username. Tokens never reach records, integration messages, telemetry, logs, exports or artifacts. Disconnect/clear token is supported, and session-only retention is the default.

items.description: Depends on WI-0029. Human/Agent/Service/Integration principals, membership in several organizations, and capability-based authorization (RecordOwnTime ... PublishBillableTime) separate from GitHub authentication. Reference-data changes need admin capabilities. Authorization diagnostics use stable CHRONA.* codes.

items.title: Chrona 06: reference data on Arca - authoritative reference records, their storage and administration across devices (CHX-040 remainder, CHX-063 remainder)
items.description: Depends on WI-0028. The pure catalogue, archive semantics, assignment rules and billing references were built in memory by WI-0045; this item makes reference data authoritative records stored through Arca (organization-scoped, shared across devices and people) and wires the CHX-063 remainder (Summa's InvoicedExternally report and ReadyForPublication staging). Also the CHX-030 remainder: organization rosters (Access.Roster) stored as records beside the reference data, members admitted and capabilities granted or revoked across devices by those who hold ManageOrganizationSettings, and choosing the organization to work in when a person belongs to several. Also the CHX-025 remainder: choosing the organization to work in when a person belongs to several, each opened from its own folder or repository.

items.title: Chrona 07: authoritative storage on Arca - partitioned layout, repository concurrency, integrity and manual edits (CHX-021, CHX-210, CHX-220, CHX-380, CHX-390, CHX-410, CHX-240 remainder, CHX-050 persistence)
items.description: Depends on WI-0028, WI-0030, arca slice 6 (GitHub adapter, ARCA-API/OUT) (GitHub adapter) and arca slice 8 (integrity, ARCA-INT) (integrity). Persist Chrona.Domain records through Arca: deterministic partitioned paths (organization/actor/year-month), bounded reads and writes, one operation as one commit, repository-state optimistic concurrency with reload, revalidation and surfaced semantic conflicts (a clean Git merge is not proof), validation of everything loaded, detection of manual edits, and an API-efficient today view. Covers scenarios 10, 31 and 32 end to end. Also the remaining evidence-reference fields (source, notes) of CHX-240. Includes persisting the full CHX-050 activity record. Also the WI-0028 remainders (CHX-024..027): read the deployment configuration and drive Storage.initializeApplication/initializeOrganization/openNamespace and Organization.read/renameOrganization through Arca's GitHub adapter from the Limen engine, store activities in each organization's folder (chrona/datasets/<OrganizationId>, its own repository when configured), and detect repository visibility from GitHub (Arca repository identity) before initializing production data. The pure persistence core (record codec, partitioned layout, change sets, integrity on load, manual-edit review, reload-and-rerun) is WI-0051; this item drives it through Arca's GitHub adapter from the Limen engine and covers the remaining API-efficiency (conditional requests, cached derived indexes, paging, rate limits, backoff) and integrity checks (receipts, publications). Token safety on the storage path (CHX-023 remainder): the GitHub adapter gets its token only from Fides' token provider (Identity.TokenProvider), reports a 401 to Fides, and no token reaches a commit, record, log or fault. Also the CHX-260 remainder of the stable diagnostics: an unresolved semantic merge conflict after reload (and, with their own items, the submitted-period restriction in WI-0036, the concurrent timer conflict in WI-0033 and the unsupported integration contract in WI-0037).

items.title: Chrona 08: offline change queue - Arca's offline queue on browser storage behind the store port, sync state and reconnect reconciliation (CHX-021, CHX-230, CHX-200 remainders)
items.description: Depends on WI-0032 and Arca's offline queue (ARCA-OFF, Arca 0.2.0). Every change is queued write-ahead in Arca's OfflineQueue, kept in this browser's localStorage through Arca's LocalStorageQueue over Limen Storage requests (IndexedDB waits on Limen), and sent in order. Network loss defers and retries with back-off; the queue survives refresh and restart and is synchronized when the records open, without blocking the first render. A queued change the repository moved under is decided again by Chrona's rules (Reconcile) and revised, or becomes a visible conflict; an unknown outcome is reconciled before anything else is sent. The queue holds operations, never record state, so it is never a competing authority: records are read from GitHub, and unsent changes are shown as unsent. Sync state is visible (CHX-230 sync state, CHX-320 sync state). Changes another account left in this browser are never sent with the current account's credential. Scenarios 31, 33 and 34. The persisted timer and concurrent timers are WI-0055. The CHX-260 remainder for the concurrent timer conflict is WI-0055. Follow-ups (2026-10-08): the move to IndexedDB is WI-0059 and the offline-start read cache is WI-0057, specified by kemiller2002/limen docs/requirements/LIMEN-INDEXEDDB-REQUIREMENTS.md (LCP-043..087) and DF-LIMEN-2026-0005; the sign-out policy is WI-0058.

items.title: Chrona 09: rebuildable derived state - indexes, totals, approval and publication projections (CHX-400)
items.description: Depends on WI-0032 and arca slice 10 (derived indexes and migration, ARCA-MIG). Every projection is rebuildable from authoritative records, and Git history is only evidence. Scenario 40. Also the CHX-220 and CHX-380 remainders: rebuildable projections and cached derived indexes (Arca Derived) so reads beyond the current period stay bounded.

items.title: Chrona 10: conflict resolution and review of outside edits in the application (CHX-260, CHX-410, CHX-320 remainders)
items.description: Depends on WI-0032 and WI-0029. Completes the write path in the application. (1) Conflict resolution: a change that could not be stored because the stored records moved is kept as a visible reconciliation obligation that names what diverged, and gets a stable diagnostic (CHX-260 remainder: unresolved semantic merge conflict). Neither side is silently discarded (23, 34). The person keeps the stored version, redoes their change on the current version, or tries again when the repository only kept moving. (2) Outside edits: the person reviews a record edited outside Chrona and accepts it from the application (CHX-410 remainder, Persistence.acceptExternalEdit). Accepting runs the same rules as a recorded activity and never grants a state the person could not reach themselves. Sign-in is done (WI-0029). The persisted timer and sync state are WI-0033. Browser reliability, accessibility end to end, quick entry and visual regression are WI-0054.

items.title: Chrona 11: timesheet periods on Arca - persisted period configuration, closed periods and their effect on submission and approval (CHX-150 remainder)
items.description: Depends on WI-0032. The pure cadences, configuration and summaries are WI-0048; this item stores the organization's period configuration and period state through Arca and enforces closed periods in submission, approval and attestation. Also the CHX-260 remainder (the submitted-period restriction's stable diagnostic), the CHX-320 remainder (the week view and submitting, approving and rejecting a period in the application) and the CHX-340 remainder (submissions, approvals and rejections in the obligations queue).

items.title: Chrona 12: consume Summa's Chrona-to-Summa billing contract through Conditor and map Chrona onto it (CHX-170, CHX-450 remainders)
items.description: Summa owns the contract (user decision 2026-10-08): summa-contracts 0.1.0 (EchelonFoundry.Summa.Contracts, wire contract summa.chrona-billing 1.0) is declared in conditor.json and installed by Conditor 0.6.0 from echelon-current 1.8.0. Chrona.Summa maps Chrona onto it: time ready for publication becomes BillableTimePublished when published (exact revision, policy, covering approval, provenance, supersedes), corrected published time that is no longer billable becomes PublicationWithdrawn, and Summa's InvoicedExternally and AdjustmentNeeded apply as Chrona's InvoiceReport and the new AdjustmentReport, only for the publication and revision Chrona recorded. Every golden vector of the package round-trips in Chrona's tests. Stored publication records, the transport and the screens are WI-0061.

items.title: Chrona 13: observation inboxes on Arca - reading producer inboxes, durable candidates and receipts, startup reconciliation (CHX-190 remainder, CHX-200, CHX-120 import path remainder, CHX-250 import audit remainder)
items.description: Depends on WI-0032. Inbox processing with overlap checks on import and audited outcomes. Scenarios 25-30. The pure processing rules are WI-0050; this item stores candidates and receipts through Arca and reads producer inboxes. Also the CHX-390 remainder for receipts: a receipt without a durable processing result is detected. The CHX-200 remainder: inbox reconciliation at startup that never blocks the first render, is resumable and paged, and where one failed item does not block the others (the queue of unsent changes already does this, WI-0033). Also CHX-180: Chrona.Integration, the contract Chrona owns as the receiver of observations (requirement 18: receiver-owned, transport-independent, versioned side by side, compatibility fixtures); it is not the Summa billing contract, which Summa owns (Chrona.Summa, WI-0037). Also the CHX-360 remainder from WI-0064: reviewing candidates is one of requirement 36's mobile priority workflows, so it is tested end to end at phone width (no sideways scrolling, 44-pixel targets).

items.title: Chrona 13a: observation processing in the pure domain - candidates, dispositions (pending, accepted, accepted with changes, rejected, duplicate, needs attention), source auto-accept policy, deduplication and receipts (CHX-190, CHX-120 import path, CHX-250 import audit; scenarios 25-30)
items.description: The storage-independent part of WI-0038, per coordinator direction 2026-10-08. TimeObservation to TimeCandidate to ProcessingReceipt as pure rules: review by default unless a source policy allows auto-accept, rejected observations preserved with reason, invalid payloads distinguishable from rejected ones, deduplication by source and observation id and by content, receipts never issued before the candidate decision exists (receipt repair), accepted activities keep source system, observation id, work item, external URL and ingestion time, imports pass the same overlap and classification rules and are audited. Inbox storage, the receiver-owned Chrona.Integration contract assembly and reconciliation stay with WI-0038 and WI-0037.

items.title: Chrona 07a: activity records on Arca - record codec, partitioned layout, change sets and integrity on load (CHX-220, CHX-390, CHX-410, CHX-050 persistence)
items.description: Split from WI-0032 (storage-free in the sense that it needs no GitHub or Fides): the pure persistence core on Arca.Core, tested against Arca's in-memory provider. The activity record codec (closed, versioned chrona.activity records), deterministic partitioned paths (organization folder / actor / year / month, stable ids, bounded month reads for the today view), change sets (one ledger command is one operation; a retimed activity that changes month moves in the same commit; every update and delete carries the revision last read), integrity on load (expansion 39: invalid JSON, schema, unsupported versions, misplaced records, duplicate ids, impossible revisions, overlapping recorded time, broken split/merge lineage; corruption is reported, never ignored), manual-edit detection from Arca commit history (41), and reload-and-revalidate after a conflict so independent changes are preserved and semantic conflicts surface (21). WI-0032 then drives this through Arca's GitHub adapter from the Limen engine.

items.title: Chrona 04b: real end-to-end sign-in against a deployed Fides exchange and GitHub App (CHX-022 remainder)
items.description: Waits on the user's deployment: Fides is not deployed anywhere yet (no AWS account, domain or GitHub App). When a Fides exchange is hosted (Fides docs/hosting/AWS.md) with Chrona registered (origin and redirect URI) and a GitHub App exists, write that deployment's chrona.deployment.json (docs/deployment-configuration.md), sign in with a real GitHub account, check the identity Chrona shows is GitHub's, that the token is kept as chosen and revoked on sign-out, that a refresh after eight hours works, and that the exchange's CORS allows exactly the deployment's origin. WI-0029 built and tested all of it against a fake exchange and GitHub; this is the check against the real ones. Also the CHX-021 check against a real repository: the records open, a first sign-in sets up the folders, commits land as one commit each with Arca's trailers, and a public production repository is refused. Also the CHX-380 remainder: measure the GitHub requests opening, reading a further month and committing take against a real repository (one request per record read, conditional requests from Arca's ETag cache, rate-limit headroom), and raise an Arca item if a month folder should be read in one batch.

items.title: Chrona 05b: bootstrap administrators from the deployment configuration; no first-opener takeover (CHX-030, CHX-027)
items.description: Security fix to WI-0031's founding rule (coordinator decision 2026-10-08): whoever first opened an organization became its administrator. Now each configured organization lists its bootstrap administrators as GitHub numeric account ids. Only a listed account can initialize an organization or become its first administrator; an empty list refuses initialization (production says so plainly); first-opener founding remains only in an explicitly local environment. An organization that already exists (WI-0032 era) whose stored roster has no administrator who is also listed is held in a 'needs administrator confirmation' state, never silently granted, that only a listed account can clear by confirming. Also documents that a dedicated Chrona data repository is the recommended setup, since any commit in a shared repository makes Chrona reload and decide again (CHX-210).

items.title: Chrona 16: visual regression against the legacy screens, closing the product UI (CHX-005 look and feel)
items.description: After WI-0062 (quick entry), WI-0063 (browser reliability) and WI-0064 (accessibility and mobile end to end), split from this item. Visual regression of Chrona's screens against the legacy time-tracking-application's look and feel as inventoried in docs/legacy (WI-0026): baseline images of each screen in light and dark, at desktop and phone width, held by the browser suite so an unintended visual change fails it.

items.title: Chrona 08b: the active timer persisted across refresh and restart, recovered at startup, and concurrent timers across devices as obligations (CHX-101, CHX-102, CHX-105, CHX-260 remainder)
items.description: Split from WI-0033, which became the offline change queue. The active timer is kept in this browser's storage per organization and person (Limen Storage, never a competing authority: it holds the device's own unfinished timer, not records), restored and recovered explicitly at startup with its elapsed time derived from its segments (Timer.recover), never silently discarded. A running timer that overlaps time another device stored since is a reconciliation obligation with a stable diagnostic (the concurrent timer conflict, requirement 26). Scenarios 4 and 9. Starting while GitHub cannot be reached: the persisted timer and this browser's unsent changes are shown and the timer keeps working; opening the records themselves offline is WI-0057 (read cache, waits on Limen IndexedDB).

items.title: Chrona 07b: store the audit trail - each command's audit entry as an immutable Arca record, read back with the activities (CHX-250, CHX-400 remainders)
items.description: Found while proving WI-0034 (every projection rebuilt from stored records): the ledger's audit trail (performer, time, source, command, prior and resulting revisions, reason, correlation id; WI-0021, WI-0023) lives only in the page's memory, so after a reload the activity screen's history is empty and nothing but Git history (supporting evidence only, requirement 40) says who changed what. Store each command's audit entry as an immutable record in the same commit as the records it audits, partitioned like the activities (actor, year, month), read with the month, and rebuild the history view from it. Revisions written before this have no stored audit entry; the view says so.

items.title: Chrona 08c: offline start with a read cache (CHX-230 remainder)
items.description: Depends on Limen's IndexedDB capability (its requirements are being written in the limen repository) and WI-0033. When GitHub cannot be reached at startup, open the organization's records from a read-only cache in IndexedDB so recording can start offline. GitHub stays the only authority: the cache is a rebuildable projection of what was last read (records with their revisions and the change token they were read at), never written to except from GitHub reads, discarded and rebuilt whenever it cannot be trusted, kept per account and organization, and cleared by the shared-device policy at sign-out. Changes made from it go through the offline queue, decided again on reconnect. No read cache on localStorage (coordinator decision 2026-10-08). Requirement 23 (CHX-230). Requirements (2026-10-08): kemiller2002/limen docs/requirements/LIMEN-INDEXEDDB-REQUIREMENTS.md LCP-082..LCP-087; DF-LIMEN-2026-0005 section 4 places the cache in Arca: a pure read-cache port in Arca.Core (Cached and Fresh are different types, so a cached value can never condition a write) with an IndexedDB adapter in EchelonFoundry.Arca.Limen (Arca WI-0021, WI-0022). Cache per account and organization the partitions already read: activities by month, the derived activity index (WI-0034), reference data and the roster, each stamped with its change token and content hashes; show them as of that token offline; revalidate the shown partitions when GitHub is reachable (refresh or mark stale). Clearing follows WI-0058's sharedDevicePolicy: discardOnSignOut clears the account's cache at sign-out; ask clears it unless the person keeps their unsent changes on this device, in which case the account's cache is kept with them (LCP-070, LCP-086). Also depends on Arca WI-0021/WI-0022 released and WI-0059.

items.title: Chrona 08d: shared-device sign-out - unsent changes are never left behind unknowingly (CHX-230, CHX-023 remainders)
items.description: Coordinator decision 2026-10-08. Signing out while this account has unsent changes in this browser asks the person to choose: send them now (when GitHub can be reached), keep them on this device for this account, or discard them after a confirmation that names how many. Nothing is lost silently and nothing is left behind unknowingly. The queue stays per account. A deployment setting sharedDevicePolicy chooses ask (the default) or discardOnSignOut, which offers only sending now or discarding. Tests for every path.

items.title: Chrona 08e: move the offline change queue from localStorage to Arca's IndexedDB adapter - one queue owner across tabs, durability mode in sync state, first-run migration (CHX-021, CHX-230, CHX-370; Limen LCP-059, LCP-065, LCP-066, LCP-070, LCP-073)
items.description: Follows WI-0033, which queues every change write-ahead in Arca's OfflineQueue on this browser's localStorage (Arca LocalStorageQueue over Limen Storage requests) and notes that IndexedDB waits on Limen; and WI-0058, whose sharedDevicePolicy (ask | discardOnSignOut) sign-out choices stay exactly as they are and are carried over to the IndexedDB queue (LCP-070). Requirements: kemiller2002/limen docs/requirements/LIMEN-INDEXEDDB-REQUIREMENTS.md LCP-059, LCP-065, LCP-066, LCP-070, LCP-073; decision DF-LIMEN-2026-0005. Depends on Arca WI-0016 and WI-0020 released (EchelonFoundry.Arca.Limen, installed through Conditor) and on Limen 0.8.0 (Limen WI-0166). Wire the IndexedDB queue store through the durability-mode composer (IndexedDb, then LocalStorage, then MemoryOnly) and show the mode wherever sync state is shown; in MemoryOnly warn before accepting an offline change. Register Limen's store and coordination packs. A second tab is told that another tab holds this device's unsent changes and can take over (OwnedElsewhere; OQ-LIMEN-IDB-001). The two-tab hazard is fixed in the interim (WI-0065, Arca 0.2.1, arca WI-0024, DF-ARCA-2026-0009). The queue is still saved as one localStorage snapshot, but Arca's LocalStorageQueue.store now fences every save on the stored text. A tab whose snapshot is stale can no longer overwrite another tab's unsent entries: its save is refused, nothing is written, the page says the change is not kept in this browser, and the change stays in that page until it is sent. StoreTests 'without Web Locks, two tabs offline in one browser' proves it. The residual gap (two tabs whose read-then-write overlap, both draining entries they loaded) is closed by WI-0067: Chrona takes the queue through LocalStorageQueue.own over Limen's coordination pack, with OwnedElsewhere shown and a hand-off on close. What remains here is the IndexedDB queue store, its durability-mode composer and first-run migration, after Limen 0.8.0; its owner (LCP-059) replaces the localStorage lock. Browser tests: two tabs, owner closed, sign-out under both policies against the IndexedDB queue, first-run migration from an existing localStorage queue.

items.title: Link Chrona's offline items to Limen's IndexedDB requirements (LCP-043..087): refine WI-0057 (read cache), capture WI-0059 (IndexedDB queue)

items.title: Chrona 12b: publication transport and stored publication records - send BillableTimePublished and PublicationWithdrawn to Summa and apply its feedback, durably (CHX-170, CHX-390, CHX-450 remainders)
items.description: Split from WI-0037, which installed Summa's contract (summa-contracts 0.1.0) and mapped Chrona onto it (Chrona.Integration.SummaBilling, golden vectors). Remaining: the review workflow's records (submissions, approvals, publication records, Summa's invoice and adjustment reports) are kept only in the page's memory and must be stored as Arca records like the activities (so a publication's source revision is checked on load, CHX-390); the transport that delivers Chrona's messages to Summa and Summa's feedback to Chrona (where Summa receives them, for example an inbox in the data repository or Summa's own endpoint, is Summa's decision); retries by publication id; and the screens to stage and publish time and to see invoiced and adjustment obligations. Scenarios 35-38. Requirements 17 (CHX-170 remainder), 45 (CHX-450 remainder) and 39 (CHX-390 remainder). Depends on the transport Summa chooses and on WI-0036 (stored submissions and approvals). Also the CHX-260 remainder: a stable CHRONA diagnostic for a message of an unsupported contract version from Summa.

items.title: Chrona 16b: browser reliability - suspension, shell updates, stale cached shell and intermittent connectivity (CHX-370)

A page suspended or hidden catches up when it returns (records refreshed, unsent changes sent, the timer display recomputed); a newer Chrona shell is detected and the person is offered a reload that cannot lose pending time; a stale cached shell never runs against a newer deployment silently; intermittent cellular connectivity backs off and recovers. Requirement 37.

Scenario 42 (mobile timer workflow), 43 (keyboard-only workflow) and 44 (screen-reader timer behaviour) end to end in a real browser; reflow at 320 CSS pixels and 400% zoom; reduced motion; weekly totals and basic sync problems reachable on a phone. iPhone VoiceOver needs a person with an iPhone: its checklist is recorded for them. Requirements 35 and 36.

Deploy Chrona to GitHub Pages in local demo mode (no Fides): Pages workflow, Pages deployment configuration, CSP meta, docs
Chrona 08f: one tab owns the unsent changes - LocalStorageQueue.own over Limen's coordination pack, hand-off on close (CHX-021, CHX-230, CHX-370)
items.description: Coordinator priority, data integrity (2026-10-08), closing WI-0059's interim gap after WI-0065 (Arca 0.2.1). Chrona selects Limen's coordination pack and takes the queue through LocalStorageQueue.own before any load, save or send. Owned: the normal path. OwnedElsewhere: the page says another tab is holding your unsent changes, keeps its own changes in the page and sends them directly while online (OQ-001), and offers to take over: a waiting lock that hands ownership off when the other tab closes, then loads and sends what that tab kept. OwnershipUnsupported: falls back to Arca's fenced store, visibly, with the mode shown, never losing data silently. A save refused because another tab wrote is said as that, not as storage the browser refuses. Tests: two tabs where only the owner sends, hand-off on close, no double send, a refused stale save. The IndexedDB move stays in WI-0059 and WI-0057, after Limen 0.8.0.

items.title: Chrona 16e: iPhone VoiceOver pass by a person, recorded against docs/accessibility-voiceover-checklist.md (CHX-350)
items.description: Split from WI-0064, which built and tested everything in requirement 35 that a browser can check (scenarios 42-44, reflow at 320 CSS pixels, reduced motion, focus kept on the control that replaced the pressed one). iPhone VoiceOver needs a person with an iPhone: they run the 14 checks in docs/accessibility-voiceover-checklist.md on a deployment, record the pass in its table (date, tester, iPhone and iOS, Chrona build), and capture a work item for each failure. CHX-350 becomes tested when a recorded pass has every row passing.
